13	# Seed 2: Implicit Spatial Occupancy Field-Guided Collision-Free Robot VLA
14	
15	Objective: CoRL 2026 submission.
16	
17	Direction: Existing VLAs lack continuous modeling capability for 3D spatial occupancy states and cannot achieve 3D spatial collision awareness while generating language-aligned actions. OccVLA (arXiv 2509.05578, September 2025) integrates 3D occupancy prediction as an implicit supervision signal into VLA, but is entirely oriented toward autonomous driving trajectory planning — the action space, sensor configuration, and task structure are fundamentally different from robot manipulation. VLSA/AEGIS (arXiv 2512.11891, December 2025) achieves VLA collision avoidance through control barrier functions, but as a plug-in safety constraint layer — the safety mechanism is independent of VLA's spatial understanding and does not affect VLA's internal spatial representation learning. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026) proves implicit 3D alignment can significantly improve VLA spatial reasoning, but does not produce explicit occupancy field representations for collision reasoning. CSSDF-Net (arXiv 2603.18669, March 2026) demonstrates the effectiveness of neural implicit distance fields in collision-free motion planning, but belongs to traditional motion planning and is completely unrelated to VLA. Core gap: No work integrates implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial representations for collision-free action generation in manipulation tasks. We propose deeply coupling implicit spatial occupancy fields with VLA, reconstructing continuous implicit occupancy fields from RGB-D data, integrating them into VLA action policy networks, enabling language-conditioned safe collision-free manipulation.
18	
19	Seed Papers:
20	- "π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control" (Black et al., Physical Intelligence, arXiv 2410.24164, October 2024)
21	  — Flow matching VLA architecture based on PaliGemma VLM, pre-trained across 8 robot platforms. Establishes the VLA general control paradigm. The base architecture for this work — adding implicit occupancy field supervision on top.
22	- "OccVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Implicit 3D Occupancy Supervision" (Liu et al., arXiv 2509.05578, September 2025)
23	  — Integrates dense 3D occupancy as prediction output and supervision signal into autonomous driving VLA, learning spatial structure from 2D vision only. Occupancy prediction serves as an implicit reasoning process, skippable at inference (zero overhead). Achieves SOTA on nuScenes trajectory planning. Core inspiration: occupancy fields can serve as VLA's implicit reasoning — but this work targets autonomous driving; our work transfers the concept to robot manipulation, needing to address action space differences (continuous joint angles vs. heading/speed) and task differences (fine grasping vs. trajectory planning).
24	- "VLSA: Vision-Language-Action Models with Plug-and-Play Safety Constraint Layer" (Hu et al., arXiv 2512.11891, December 2025)
25	  — Proposes AEGIS plug-and-play safety constraint layer, using control barrier functions, identifying obstacles through open-set object detection + depth maps, externally constraining VLA actions. Improves collision avoidance by 59.16% on SafeLIBERO benchmark. Core contrast: Safety is a post-processing layer that does not affect VLA's internal spatial understanding — our work internalizes occupancy awareness into the VLA architecture, giving the model collision consciousness during action generation.
26	- "Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-language-action Model" (Li et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276)
27	  — Implicitly aligns VLA intermediate-layer visual embeddings with 3D foundation model geometric representations, without explicit 3D input. Surpasses all 2D and 3D VLA baselines, with 3.8× training acceleration. Methodological foundation: proves implicit 3D alignment's effectiveness in VLA — our work further specializes the alignment target from general 3D geometry to occupancy fields, specifically serving collision awareness.
28	- "Neural Grasp Distance Fields for Robot Manipulation" (Weng et al., Meta AI / CMU, ICRA 2023, arXiv 2211.02647)
29	  — Represents grasps as neural distance fields: input 6D end-effector pose, output distance to valid grasp manifold. The continuous differentiable field is directly embedded in trajectory optimization, considering both collision avoidance and smoothness constraints. Execution success rate exceeds baselines by 63%. Validates implicit field representations' effectiveness in robot manipulation — but belongs to traditional motion planning (not VLA); our work embeds the implicit field concept into VLA architecture.

32	- OccVLA integrates occupancy fields into VLA but targets autonomous driving, with fundamentally different action spaces and task structures from robot manipulation
33	- AEGIS/VLSA achieves VLA collision avoidance but as a plug-in safety layer, not changing VLA's internal spatial representation
34	- SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2503.03480) uses constrained Markov decision processes for VLA safety alignment, an RL-based method, not geometric/occupancy-based
35	- Spatial Forcing does implicit 3D alignment but does not produce occupancy fields, not targeting collision reasoning
36	- CSSDF-Net, Neural Grasp Distance Fields validate implicit fields' effectiveness in collision avoidance but are not VLA
37	- No work integrates implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial priors for manipulation task collision awareness
38	
39	In Scope: Methods integrating implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial representations for collision-free manipulation. Specifically includes: implicit occupancy field encoder design based on RGB-D, fusion mechanism between occupancy field features and VLA action policy, occupancy field supervised training strategy (OccVLA-style auxiliary task design adapted for manipulation), online occupancy field updating for dynamic objects, comparison between collision-aware action generation and traditional collision checking.
40	
41	Out of Scope: Autonomous driving scenarios (OccVLA/SparseOccVLA already done). Plug-in safety constraint layers (AEGIS already done). RL-based safety alignment (SafeVLA already done). Implicit fields in traditional motion planning (CSSDF-Net, NGDF already done). 3D VLA improvements not involving collision avoidance (Spatial Forcing, 3DS-VLA already done). Pure benchmarking.
42	
43	Contribution Type: Method contribution. Output must include (1) architecture design for implicit occupancy field and VLA fusion, (2) occupancy field supervised training strategy, (3) experimental validation of collision avoidance on manipulation tasks, demonstrating advantages over plug-in safety layers and occupancy-free VLAs.
44	
45	Evaluation Protocol:
46	Training: Fine-tune based on π0/OpenVLA architecture, adding implicit occupancy field branch. Training data uses LIBERO + ManiSkill2/3 simulation data (with collision annotations).
47	Evaluation Metrics:
48	- Primary metric: Joint metric of manipulation task success rate × collision-free rate
49	- Collision rate: Number/frequency of collisions with environmental objects during task execution
50	- Manipulation success rate: Task completion rate (cannot sacrifice too much success rate for safety)
51	- Trajectory smoothness: L2 norm of joint angle accelerations
52	- Baseline comparisons:
53	  1. Collision-unaware VLA (OpenVLA/π0 direct fine-tuning)
54	  2. Plug-in safety layer (AEGIS/VLSA reproduction)
55	  3. Explicit depth collision checking + VLA
56	  4. RL safety alignment (SafeVLA approach)
57	  5. Traditional motion planning + VLA goals (VoxPoser approach)
58	- Ablation studies: Occupancy field supervision vs. depth supervision vs. no 3D supervision, internal occupancy vs. plug-in occupancy, online update vs. static occupancy field
59	- Scene complexity tests: Sparse scenes → dense cluttered scenes → dynamic object scenes
60	- Real robot validation: Validate collision avoidance capability on at least 1 real robot platform
61	
62	Building Blocks: π0/OpenVLA codebase (VLA base architecture); OccVLA codebase (occupancy field supervision method reference, needs adaptation to manipulation domain); AEGIS codebase (plug-in safety layer baseline); Spatial Forcing codebase (implicit 3D alignment method reference); LIBERO benchmark (manipulation task evaluation); ManiSkill2/3 simulation platform (with collision physics simulation); SafeLIBERO benchmark (collision avoidance evaluation); Occ3D/SurroundOcc (occupancy field GT generation reference).
63	
64	Hard Constraints:
65	Compute: ≤200 H100-hours. Strategy: Fine-tune based on 7B VLA, lightweight occupancy field branch (OccVLA-style skippable-at-inference design). Simulation training ~80 H100-hours, baseline reproduction ~40 H100-hours, ablation ~40 H100-hours, real robot experiments ~40 H100-hours.
66	Evaluation: Must validate collision avoidance on manipulation tasks (not driving). Must include ≥4 baselines. Must report both success rate and collision rate (cannot report only one). Must include ablation and scene complexity experiments. Real robot validation recommended.
67	
68	Exploration Directions: (1) OccVLA-style occupancy auxiliary task transfer to manipulation: OccVLA proves occupancy prediction can serve as VLA auxiliary task to improve spatial understanding. Transfer the same design to manipulation VLA: predict 3D occupancy voxels of the workspace during training, serving as implicit reasoning at inference (optionally skippable). Key adaptations: manipulation scene occupancy scale (centimeter-level precision vs. driving's meter-level), joint-space collision vs. Cartesian-space collision. (2) Occupancy field gradient-guided action correction: Implicit occupancy fields are continuous differentiable functions — after action generation, backpropagate through occupancy field gradients to correct actions away from collision regions. Similar to Neural Grasp Distance Fields using distance field gradients for trajectory optimization, but our work does gradient correction in VLA's action token space rather than joint space. (3) Internal vs. plug-in comparison framework: Design rigorous comparative experiments proving internalized occupancy awareness outperforms plug-in safety layers — the core argument is that the internalized approach enables "anticipatory avoidance" (generating trajectories inherently far from obstacles), while plug-in approaches can only "post-hoc correct" (truncating/modifying already-generated unsafe actions). (4) Multi-granularity occupancy representation: Coarse-grained (room-level traversable regions) → medium-grained (tabletop cluttered object distribution) → fine-grained (precise geometry around grasped objects), VLA attends to different granularities at different decision stages. (5) Self-supervised occupancy field pre-training: Pre-train occupancy field encoder on large-scale RGB-D data (no action annotation needed), then connect to VLA fine-tuning. Occupancy fields are purely geometric properties, learnable from abundant 3D data, not dependent on expensive robot demonstration data.

71	- Validating only in autonomous driving scenarios — OccVLA/SparseOccVLA already done; must validate on manipulation tasks
72	- Plug-in occupancy field post-processing — duplicates AEGIS approach; core contribution is internalizing occupancy awareness into VLA
73	- Overly complex occupancy field reconstruction (e.g., full NeRF) causing unacceptable inference latency — needs lightweight design

75	- Ignoring SafeVLA — NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, RL-based safety method; must clarify differences between geometric and RL approaches

109	## Core Problem
110	
111	Despite a proliferation of 3D-aware VLA methods (DepthVLA, QDepth-VLA, GeoAware-VLA, SpatialVLA, Evo-0, StemVLA, SA-VLA, ST-VLA, 3DS-VLA, Spatial Forcing, GST-VLA, 3D-CAVLA, AugVLA-3D, Evo-Depth) that improve general spatial reasoning through depth, geometry, or point cloud representations, none explicitly targets collision avoidance in cluttered manipulation. These methods optimize for task success rate, viewpoint generalization, or grasping precision — not collision metrics. Meanwhile, the only collision-safe VLAs (AEGIS/VLSA, CoFreeVLA, SafeVLA) achieve safety via post-hoc mechanisms — control barrier functions that externally correct trajectories, risk estimators that halt unsafe actions, or reward shaping via constrained MDPs — without improving the model's internal collision geometry understanding. The result: 3D-aware VLAs still collide in cluttered scenes, and collision-safe VLAs don't internalize spatial understanding. No existing work provides a differentiable collision-aware mechanism that operates within the VLA forward pass to jointly generate actions and reason about collision geometry.
112	
113	## Opportunity / Why Now
114	
115	The disjunction between 'spatially-aware VLAs' and 'collision-safe VLAs' creates a precise research gap at their intersection. Three observations motivate our approach: (1) Depth-as-auxiliary-supervision (QDepth-VLA) provides camera-frame 2.5D information — 'how far is each pixel from the camera' — which improves spatial reasoning but does not directly encode collision geometry, and its gradients live in image space requiring implicit perspective-to-workspace transformation. (2) Post-hoc safety methods (AEGIS CBF, CoFreeVLA risk estimation) correct or halt trajectories at inference but leave the VLA's internal representations collision-ignorant, creating a disconnect between the model's reasoning and the safety layer. (3) Workspace signed distance fields (SDFs) provide a fundamentally different and collision-native signal: 'how close is each 3D point to the nearest obstacle surface,' with gradients pointing directly toward collision-free directions in workspace frame — no coordinate transformation needed. Crucially, SDF gradients are differentiable and can flow back into action token generation during the forward pass, enabling collision-aware action generation rather than post-hoc correction. SDF is the native representation for collision checking in robotics planning (iSDF, CSSDF-Net, SAMP, ReDSDF, Neural NMPC-SDF), and recent work (SAMP, Prof. Robot) demonstrates that differentiable SDF gradients can be integrated into learned policies for collision reduction — but none of these are VLA methods. The 'why now': (a) SafeLIBERO (Dec 2025) provides the first collision-specific VLA benchmark with 32 scenarios and 1600 episodes, yet only AEGIS has been evaluated there; (b) MuJoCo 3+ natively supports SDF computation from meshes, reducing implementation barriers; (c) DFM-VLA (Mar 2026) demonstrates that iterative action refinement within VLA is feasible and effective — our SDF-gradient refinement provides a collision-specific instantiation of this paradigm.
116	
117	## Landscape (SOTA & Limitations)
118	
119	3D-AWARE VLAs (improve spatial reasoning, do NOT target collision avoidance): DepthVLA (arXiv 2510.13375, Oct 2025) integrates a pretrained depth transformer via mixture-of-transformers, achieving 94.9% on LIBERO but not evaluated on collision metrics. QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836, Oct 2025) uses quantized depth prediction as VLA auxiliary supervision via VQ-VAE — the closest methodological precedent for auxiliary-task supervision, operating in 2.5D camera frame without collision-awareness; open-source on GitHub. GeoAware-VLA (arXiv 2509.14117, Sep 2025) injects pretrained geometric vision model features for viewpoint invariance. 3D-CAVLA (arXiv 2505.05800, May 2025) enhances task generalization via chain-of-thought reasoning, depth-aware perception, and ROI detection, achieving 98.1% on LIBERO in-domain; open-source on GitHub. AugVLA-3D (arXiv 2602.10698, Feb 2026, ICRA 2026) uses VGGT for depth-driven 3D feature augmentation with geometry-aware routing and action-assistant regularization. Evo-0 (arXiv 2507.00416, Jul 2025) uses VGGT geometric foundation model for implicit 3D understanding. SpatialVLA (arXiv 2501.15830, Jan 2025) introduces Ego3D position encoding. StemVLA (arXiv 2602.23721, Feb 2026) forecasts future 3D spatial geometry. SA-VLA (arXiv 2602.00743, Jan 2026) fuses implicit spatial representations for RL fine-tuning. ST-VLA (arXiv 2603.13788, Mar 2026) enables 4D spatiotemporal understanding. 3DS-VLA (2025) adds 2D-to-3D positional alignment. Evo-Depth (arXiv 2605.14950, May 2026) proposes lightweight depth-enhanced VLA. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276) proves implicit 3D alignment accelerates VLA training 3.8×. GST-VLA (arXiv 2603.09079, Mar 2026) uses Gaussian spatial tokens. COLLISION-SAFE VLAs (target collision avoidance but externalize safety): AEGIS/VLSA (arXiv 2512.11891, Dec 2025) is the only published collision-safe manipulation VLA, achieving 77.85% CAR on SafeLIBERO via plug-in CBF — but safety is post-hoc correction, not internalized reasoning. CoFreeVLA (arXiv 2601.21712, Jan 2026) addresses dual-arm self-collision via risk estimation, not obstacle avoidance. SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2503.03480) uses constrained MDPs for safety alignment via reward shaping, not geometric reasoning. ACTION REFINEMENT VLAs: DFM-VLA (arXiv 2603.26320, Mar 2026) demonstrates iterative action token refinement via discrete flow matching on LIBERO (95.7% success) — establishes feasibility of within-VLA action refinement but without collision-specific guidance. DIFFERENTIABLE SDF IN ROBOTICS (not VLA): SAMP (arXiv 2509.11185, Sep 2025) fuses robot+environment SDF on spatial anchors for neural motion policy with 7% collision reduction — demonstrates SDF-gradient-guided policy learning but is not a VLA. CSSDF-Net (arXiv 2603.18669, Mar 2026) learns C-space SDF for trajectory optimization. Prof. Robot (CVPR 2025, arXiv 2503.11269) uses differentiable SDF for collision-free robot rendering with 99% collision reduction. iSDF (RSS 2022) provides real-time neural SDF. ReDSDF (IROS 2022) demonstrates regularized deep SDFs for reactive motion generation. Neural NMPC-SDF (IJRR 2025, arXiv 2511.21312) encodes range images into SDF for NMPC collision avoidance. CDFlow (arXiv 2509.13771) learns C-space distance field via Neural ODEs. GAP CONFIRMED: No published work integrates differentiable signed distance fields into VLA architecture for collision-aware action generation. The gap is specifically at the intersection of: (a) differentiable SDF-gradient-guided action generation (proven in non-VLA robotics: SAMP, Prof. Robot, ReDSDF), (b) auxiliary 3D supervision within VLA (proven for depth: QDepth-VLA), and (c) collision-specific VLA evaluation (SafeLIBERO). The April 2026 VLA safety survey (arXiv 2604.23775) confirms this gap.
120	
121	## Proposed Approach
122	
123	We propose ColliForce-VLA, whose primary contribution is a differentiable collision-aware action generation mechanism for VLAs, enabled by a learned workspace SDF that provides gradient-based collision guidance within the forward pass — not merely auxiliary supervision during training and not post-hoc trajectory correction. This is architecturally distinct from both QDepth-VLA (training-only auxiliary loss) and AEGIS (external CBF correction). Key insight: While depth auxiliary tasks (QDepth-VLA) teach the model 'how far each pixel is from the camera' with gradients in image space, our learned SDF predicts 'how close each 3D workspace point is to the nearest obstacle surface' with gradients in workspace frame — and crucially, these SDF gradients can flow back through the action generation pathway during the forward pass, directly modulating action tokens toward collision-free configurations. Architecture — three components with distinct roles: (1) SDF Decoder with Action-Gradient Coupling: A cross-attention decoder takes intermediate VLA backbone features (from π0 via openpi or OpenVLA-OFT) and predicts signed distance at sparse 3D query points (2048 points, importance-sampled near robot workspace and object surfaces). Ground-truth SDF is extracted from LIBERO/SafeLIBERO MuJoCo visual geometry meshes (OBJ/STL assets, not simplified collision convex hulls) using established mesh-to-SDF libraries (trimesh proximity queries, pysdf). Critical design choice: the SDF decoder shares intermediate representations with the action head via a bidirectional cross-attention bridge — SDF features inform action generation, and action token positions define where SDF is most needed. This creates an architectural coupling absent in QDepth-VLA's purely auxiliary decoder. (2) SDF-Gradient-Guided Action Refinement (PRIMARY NOVELTY): During the forward pass, predicted SDF values at candidate end-effector positions (derived from action tokens) are used to compute workspace-frame collision gradients via backpropagation through the SDF decoder. These gradients are projected back into the action token space through a learned linear projection, producing a collision-avoidance correction that is added to the action tokens before the final action head output. This is a single differentiable forward pass — not iterative post-hoc correction. The mechanism is end-to-end trainable: the SDF decoder learns to produce gradients that, when projected into action space, reduce collisions. Theoretical basis: ∇SDF at a point in workspace directly points away from the nearest obstacle surface (by definition of SDF), providing geometrically meaningful collision-avoidance direction. In contrast, depth gradients in camera frame encode ∂depth/∂pixel, which requires an implicit perspective-to-workspace coordinate transformation (involving camera intrinsics, extrinsics, and nonlinear projection) to yield collision-relevant workspace directions — this transformation degrades gradient quality, especially for oblique viewing angles and occluded regions. (3) SDF Auxiliary Loss (SECONDARY): Standard SDF prediction loss during training forces the backbone to internalize full 3D collision geometry including occluded regions. This provides the representational foundation for component (2) but is explicitly secondary — the key contribution is how SDF gradients modulate action generation, not the auxiliary loss itself. Training: Joint optimization of action prediction loss, SDF prediction loss, and an SDF-gradient alignment loss that encourages the gradient correction to reduce predicted collision probability. The gradient alignment loss is key: it ensures the learned SDF-to-action-space projection produces corrections that actually improve collision avoidance, not just minimize SDF prediction error. Evaluation strategy — two tiers: Tier 1 (Standard): SafeLIBERO (32 collision scenarios, 1600 episodes) measuring both collision avoidance rate (CAR) and task success rate (TSR), plus standard LIBERO suites to verify no regression. Tier 2 (Stress Tests — isolating SDF advantages over depth): We design supplementary scenarios in MuJoCo/LIBERO that specifically test SDF's claimed advantages: (a) Occluded-obstacle scenarios: obstacles placed behind the robot arm invisible to the single camera — depth cannot perceive them, SDF from 3D workspace knowledge can; (b) Dense-corridor scenarios: end-effector must navigate between closely packed objects where depth map gradients blur across multiple surfaces while SDF encodes distance to ALL nearby surfaces simultaneously; (c) Multi-angle proximity: scenarios where the camera viewing angle creates depth ambiguities (nearly parallel surfaces at similar depth) that SDF naturally resolves. These stress tests are designed so that if SDF wins convincingly on them — even with marginal gains on standard SafeLIBERO — the paper tells a compelling story about when and why SDF matters. Critical baselines: (1) QDepth-VLA (open-source GitHub) — depth-as-auxiliary-supervision, our closest methodological comparator and primary depth baseline; (2) AEGIS/VLSA — post-hoc CBF approach, current SOTA on SafeLIBERO; (3) Vanilla VLA (OpenVLA-OFT, π0) — no spatial auxiliary supervision; (4) Spatial Forcing — general 3D alignment; (5) DepthVLA — if code becomes available, otherwise secondary to QDepth-VLA. Key ablations: (A1) SDF auxiliary supervision only (no gradient-guided action generation) — isolates training-time benefit, directly comparable to 'QDepth-VLA with SDF target swap'; (A2) SDF-gradient-guided action generation only (no auxiliary loss during training, decoder trained separately then frozen) — isolates inference-time mechanism; (A3) Full ColliForce-VLA (both) — demonstrates synergy; (A4) SDF vs. depth vs. binary occupancy as auxiliary target, all with gradient-guided action generation — tests whether SDF gradients are specifically better than depth/occupancy gradients for collision avoidance; (A5) Ablation on SDF ground-truth source: visual mesh vs. collision convex hull — validates our design choice. Advantages of SDF-gradient-guided action generation over alternatives: (a) Workspace-frame gradients directly aligned with robot motion — no coordinate transformation needed; (b) Full 3D coverage including occluded regions; (c) Continuous, geometrically meaningful gradients — ∇SDF points away from obstacles by construction; binary occupancy has zero gradient almost everywhere; (d) Single forward pass — no iterative refinement or external correction loop; (e) End-to-end trainable — the entire pathway from SDF prediction to action correction is differentiable.
124

# Idea Brief: Differentiable Collision-Aware Action Generation via Learned Workspace SDF for Vision-Language-Action Models


- **Idea ID**: `idea_022`

## Seed Topic

# Seed 2: Implicit Spatial Occupancy Field-Guided Collision-Free Robot VLA

Objective: CoRL 2026 submission.

Direction: Existing VLAs lack continuous modeling capability for 3D spatial occupancy states and cannot achieve 3D spatial collision awareness while generating language-aligned actions. OccVLA (arXiv 2509.05578, September 2025) integrates 3D occupancy prediction as an implicit supervision signal into VLA, but is entirely oriented toward autonomous driving trajectory planning — the action space, sensor configuration, and task structure are fundamentally different from robot manipulation. VLSA/AEGIS (arXiv 2512.11891, December 2025) achieves VLA collision avoidance through control barrier functions, but as a plug-in safety constraint layer — the safety mechanism is independent of VLA's spatial understanding and does not affect VLA's internal spatial representation learning. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026) proves implicit 3D alignment can significantly improve VLA spatial reasoning, but does not produce explicit occupancy field representations for collision reasoning. CSSDF-Net (arXiv 2603.18669, March 2026) demonstrates the effectiveness of neural implicit distance fields in collision-free motion planning, but belongs to traditional motion planning and is completely unrelated to VLA. Core gap: No work integrates implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial representations for collision-free action generation in manipulation tasks. We propose deeply coupling implicit spatial occupancy fields with VLA, reconstructing continuous implicit occupancy fields from RGB-D data, integrating them into VLA action policy networks, enabling language-conditioned safe collision-free manipulation.

Seed Papers:
- "π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control" (Black et al., Physical Intelligence, arXiv 2410.24164, October 2024)
  — Flow matching VLA architecture based on PaliGemma VLM, pre-trained across 8 robot platforms. Establishes the VLA general control paradigm. The base architecture for this work — adding implicit occupancy field supervision on top.
- "OccVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Implicit 3D Occupancy Supervision" (Liu et al., arXiv 2509.05578, September 2025)
  — Integrates dense 3D occupancy as prediction output and supervision signal into autonomous driving VLA, learning spatial structure from 2D vision only. Occupancy prediction serves as an implicit reasoning process, skippable at inference (zero overhead). Achieves SOTA on nuScenes trajectory planning. Core inspiration: occupancy fields can serve as VLA's implicit reasoning — but this work targets autonomous driving; our work transfers the concept to robot manipulation, needing to address action space differences (continuous joint angles vs. heading/speed) and task differences (fine grasping vs. trajectory planning).
- "VLSA: Vision-Language-Action Models with Plug-and-Play Safety Constraint Layer" (Hu et al., arXiv 2512.11891, December 2025)
  — Proposes AEGIS plug-and-play safety constraint layer, using control barrier functions, identifying obstacles through open-set object detection + depth maps, externally constraining VLA actions. Improves collision avoidance by 59.16% on SafeLIBERO benchmark. Core contrast: Safety is a post-processing layer that does not affect VLA's internal spatial understanding — our work internalizes occupancy awareness into the VLA architecture, giving the model collision consciousness during action generation.
- "Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-language-action Model" (Li et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276)
  — Implicitly aligns VLA intermediate-layer visual embeddings with 3D foundation model geometric representations, without explicit 3D input. Surpasses all 2D and 3D VLA baselines, with 3.8× training acceleration. Methodological foundation: proves implicit 3D alignment's effectiveness in VLA — our work further specializes the alignment target from general 3D geometry to occupancy fields, specifically serving collision awareness.
- "Neural Grasp Distance Fields for Robot Manipulation" (Weng et al., Meta AI / CMU, ICRA 2023, arXiv 2211.02647)
  — Represents grasps as neural distance fields: input 6D end-effector pose, output distance to valid grasp manifold. The continuous differentiable field is directly embedded in trajectory optimization, considering both collision avoidance and smoothness constraints. Execution success rate exceeds baselines by 63%. Validates implicit field representations' effectiveness in robot manipulation — but belongs to traditional motion planning (not VLA); our work embeds the implicit field concept into VLA architecture.

Known Gap:
- OccVLA integrates occupancy fields into VLA but targets autonomous driving, with fundamentally different action spaces and task structures from robot manipulation
- AEGIS/VLSA achieves VLA collision avoidance but as a plug-in safety layer, not changing VLA's internal spatial representation
- SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2503.03480) uses constrained Markov decision processes for VLA safety alignment, an RL-based method, not geometric/occupancy-based
- Spatial Forcing does implicit 3D alignment but does not produce occupancy fields, not targeting collision reasoning
- CSSDF-Net, Neural Grasp Distance Fields validate implicit fields' effectiveness in collision avoidance but are not VLA
- No work integrates implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial priors for manipulation task collision awareness

In Scope: Methods integrating implicit occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial representations for collision-free manipulation. Specifically includes: implicit occupancy field encoder design based on RGB-D, fusion mechanism between occupancy field features and VLA action policy, occupancy field supervised training strategy (OccVLA-style auxiliary task design adapted for manipulation), online occupancy field updating for dynamic objects, comparison between collision-aware action generation and traditional collision checking.

Out of Scope: Autonomous driving scenarios (OccVLA/SparseOccVLA already done). Plug-in safety constraint layers (AEGIS already done). RL-based safety alignment (SafeVLA already done). Implicit fields in traditional motion planning (CSSDF-Net, NGDF already done). 3D VLA improvements not involving collision avoidance (Spatial Forcing, 3DS-VLA already done). Pure benchmarking.

Contribution Type: Method contribution. Output must include (1) architecture design for implicit occupancy field and VLA fusion, (2) occupancy field supervised training strategy, (3) experimental validation of collision avoidance on manipulation tasks, demonstrating advantages over plug-in safety layers and occupancy-free VLAs.

Evaluation Protocol:
Training: Fine-tune based on π0/OpenVLA architecture, adding implicit occupancy field branch. Training data uses LIBERO + ManiSkill2/3 simulation data (with collision annotations).
Evaluation Metrics:
- Primary metric: Joint metric of manipulation task success rate × collision-free rate
- Collision rate: Number/frequency of collisions with environmental objects during task execution
- Manipulation success rate: Task completion rate (cannot sacrifice too much success rate for safety)
- Trajectory smoothness: L2 norm of joint angle accelerations
- Baseline comparisons:
  1. Collision-unaware VLA (OpenVLA/π0 direct fine-tuning)
  2. Plug-in safety layer (AEGIS/VLSA reproduction)
  3. Explicit depth collision checking + VLA
  4. RL safety alignment (SafeVLA approach)
  5. Traditional motion planning + VLA goals (VoxPoser approach)
- Ablation studies: Occupancy field supervision vs. depth supervision vs. no 3D supervision, internal occupancy vs. plug-in occupancy, online update vs. static occupancy field
- Scene complexity tests: Sparse scenes → dense cluttered scenes → dynamic object scenes
- Real robot validation: Validate collision avoidance capability on at least 1 real robot platform

Building Blocks: π0/OpenVLA codebase (VLA base architecture); OccVLA codebase (occupancy field supervision method reference, needs adaptation to manipulation domain); AEGIS codebase (plug-in safety layer baseline); Spatial Forcing codebase (implicit 3D alignment method reference); LIBERO benchmark (manipulation task evaluation); ManiSkill2/3 simulation platform (with collision physics simulation); SafeLIBERO benchmark (collision avoidance evaluation); Occ3D/SurroundOcc (occupancy field GT generation reference).

Hard Constraints:
Compute: ≤200 H100-hours. Strategy: Fine-tune based on 7B VLA, lightweight occupancy field branch (OccVLA-style skippable-at-inference design). Simulation training ~80 H100-hours, baseline reproduction ~40 H100-hours, ablation ~40 H100-hours, real robot experiments ~40 H100-hours.
Evaluation: Must validate collision avoidance on manipulation tasks (not driving). Must include ≥4 baselines. Must report both success rate and collision rate (cannot report only one). Must include ablation and scene complexity experiments. Real robot validation recommended.

Exploration Directions: (1) OccVLA-style occupancy auxiliary task transfer to manipulation: OccVLA proves occupancy prediction can serve as VLA auxiliary task to improve spatial understanding. Transfer the same design to manipulation VLA: predict 3D occupancy voxels of the workspace during training, serving as implicit reasoning at inference (optionally skippable). Key adaptations: manipulation scene occupancy scale (centimeter-level precision vs. driving's meter-level), joint-space collision vs. Cartesian-space collision. (2) Occupancy field gradient-guided action correction: Implicit occupancy fields are continuous differentiable functions — after action generation, backpropagate through occupancy field gradients to correct actions away from collision regions. Similar to Neural Grasp Distance Fields using distance field gradients for trajectory optimization, but our work does gradient correction in VLA's action token space rather than joint space. (3) Internal vs. plug-in comparison framework: Design rigorous comparative experiments proving internalized occupancy awareness outperforms plug-in safety layers — the core argument is that the internalized approach enables "anticipatory avoidance" (generating trajectories inherently far from obstacles), while plug-in approaches can only "post-hoc correct" (truncating/modifying already-generated unsafe actions). (4) Multi-granularity occupancy representation: Coarse-grained (room-level traversable regions) → medium-grained (tabletop cluttered object distribution) → fine-grained (precise geometry around grasped objects), VLA attends to different granularities at different decision stages. (5) Self-supervised occupancy field pre-training: Pre-train occupancy field encoder on large-scale RGB-D data (no action annotation needed), then connect to VLA fine-tuning. Occupancy fields are purely geometric properties, learnable from abundant 3D data, not dependent on expensive robot demonstration data.

Avoid:
- Validating only in autonomous driving scenarios — OccVLA/SparseOccVLA already done; must validate on manipulation tasks
- Plug-in occupancy field post-processing — duplicates AEGIS approach; core contribution is internalizing occupancy awareness into VLA
- Overly complex occupancy field reconstruction (e.g., full NeRF) causing unacceptable inference latency — needs lightweight design
- Ignoring AEGIS baseline — it is currently the only published collision-safe VLA work; must directly compare
- Ignoring SafeVLA — NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, RL-based safety method; must clarify differences between geometric and RL approaches
- Reporting only collision rate without success rate — a robot that never moves has zero collision rate but is useless
- Testing only in simple obstacle-free environments — must include dense cluttered and dynamic scenes

Idea Generation Quality Constraints (Hard rules based on historical cases):

1. No strawman problems: Any claim of "existing methods assume X" or "existing methods fail on Y" must cite specific paragraphs from specific papers as evidence. Must not fabricate mainstream assumptions based on pre-training knowledge.

2. No pure observation ideas: "We discover phenomenon X" is not a contribution. Discovering a problem is not a contribution — solving the problem is. Output must include a complete method, not merely analysis/benchmark/empirical study.

3. No mediocre methods: Methods must answer:
   - Core insight: OccVLA proves occupancy prediction can serve as VLA's implicit reasoning process to improve spatial understanding, but was only validated in autonomous driving. We find the same principle can transfer to manipulation — but needs to address precision scale differences (centimeter-level vs. meter-level) and action space differences (joint angles vs. heading), and manipulation scene collision structures (fine obstacle avoidance among densely cluttered objects) are fundamentally different from driving (large-scale avoidance on open roads).
   - Why non-obvious: (1) OccVLA only appeared in September 2025; the occupancy + VLA concept itself is very new; (2) transfer from driving to manipulation is non-trivial — action spaces, precision requirements, and scene structures are completely different; (3) AEGIS (December 2025) took the plug-in route rather than internalization, suggesting the internalized design is not obvious.
   - What information is exploited: Continuous implicit occupancy fields provide dense 3D spatial traversability information — the plug-in safety layer (AEGIS) only utilizes sparse object detection + depth, unable to sense continuous spatial occupancy states.
   - Mechanistic argument: Internalized occupancy fields let VLA "see" 3D spatial occupancy states during action generation, thus generating trajectories inherently far from collision regions (anticipatory avoidance). Plug-in methods can only detect and correct collisions after action generation, which is reactive — this is worse in dense cluttered scenes because the "safe correction space" is small.

4. No duplicating existing work: Each core technical component must be confirmed with at least 3 different search queries to have no directly related work.

5. No padding experiments:
   - "Delete experiment test": Keep only the method description — does it teach the reader something non-trivial? Yes — implicit occupancy fields can be internalized into VLA for anticipatory collision avoidance.
   - "Baseline fear test": If the AEGIS plug-in layer performs similarly, is the paper still valuable? Must prove the internalized approach outperforms plug-in methods in dense cluttered scenes.
   - "Citation test": Will people cite the numbers or the insight 5 years later? The insight — occupancy fields as VLA internal spatial priors paradigm.

6. The following method patterns are rejected (unless with extremely strong structural reasons):
   - "Add module X" — Why this specific structure?
   - "Train on data Y" — Is data construction itself a contribution?
   - "Transfer Z from domain A to domain B" — What is the structural analogy between A and B? Must clearly explain non-trivial adaptation design in the driving-to-manipulation transfer.
   - "Combine P and Q" — Where is the synergy?
   - "Use more/larger/stronger X" — Scale is not a method contribution.

Competition Warning: OccVLA (September 2025) is conceptually closest — integrates occupancy into VLA but targets driving. SparseOccVLA (January 2026, arXiv 2601.06474) is also in the driving domain. AEGIS/VLSA (December 2025) is the only published collision-safe VLA manipulation work but takes the plug-in route. SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2503.03480) uses RL for VLA safety alignment. 3DS-VLA (CoRL 2025) does 3D spatial-aware VLA manipulation but does not involve collision avoidance. GeoVLA (arXiv 2508.09071) enhances VLA with point clouds but does not involve collision. Differentiation core: The only work internalizing implicit occupancy fields into VLA architecture for manipulation collision awareness — distinct from driving (OccVLA) and plug-in (AEGIS) approaches. Monitor: OccVLA author team (whether they will extend to manipulation), AEGIS author team (whether they will internalize the safety layer), Spatial Forcing author team.

## Core Problem

Despite a proliferation of 3D-aware VLA methods (DepthVLA, QDepth-VLA, GeoAware-VLA, SpatialVLA, Evo-0, StemVLA, SA-VLA, ST-VLA, 3DS-VLA, Spatial Forcing, GST-VLA, 3D-CAVLA, AugVLA-3D, Evo-Depth) that improve general spatial reasoning through depth, geometry, or point cloud representations, none explicitly targets collision avoidance in cluttered manipulation. These methods optimize for task success rate, viewpoint generalization, or grasping precision — not collision metrics. Meanwhile, the only collision-safe VLAs (AEGIS/VLSA, CoFreeVLA, SafeVLA) achieve safety via post-hoc mechanisms — control barrier functions that externally correct trajectories, risk estimators that halt unsafe actions, or reward shaping via constrained MDPs — without improving the model's internal collision geometry understanding. The result: 3D-aware VLAs still collide in cluttered scenes, and collision-safe VLAs don't internalize spatial understanding. No existing work provides a differentiable collision-aware mechanism that operates within the VLA forward pass to jointly generate actions and reason about collision geometry.

## Opportunity / Why Now

The disjunction between 'spatially-aware VLAs' and 'collision-safe VLAs' creates a precise research gap at their intersection. Three observations motivate our approach: (1) Depth-as-auxiliary-supervision (QDepth-VLA) provides camera-frame 2.5D information — 'how far is each pixel from the camera' — which improves spatial reasoning but does not directly encode collision geometry, and its gradients live in image space requiring implicit perspective-to-workspace transformation. (2) Post-hoc safety methods (AEGIS CBF, CoFreeVLA risk estimation) correct or halt trajectories at inference but leave the VLA's internal representations collision-ignorant, creating a disconnect between the model's reasoning and the safety layer. (3) Workspace signed distance fields (SDFs) provide a fundamentally different and collision-native signal: 'how close is each 3D point to the nearest obstacle surface,' with gradients pointing directly toward collision-free directions in workspace frame — no coordinate transformation needed. Crucially, SDF gradients are differentiable and can flow back into action token generation during the forward pass, enabling collision-aware action generation rather than post-hoc correction. SDF is the native representation for collision checking in robotics planning (iSDF, CSSDF-Net, SAMP, ReDSDF, Neural NMPC-SDF), and recent work (SAMP, Prof. Robot) demonstrates that differentiable SDF gradients can be integrated into learned policies for collision reduction — but none of these are VLA methods. The 'why now': (a) SafeLIBERO (Dec 2025) provides the first collision-specific VLA benchmark with 32 scenarios and 1600 episodes, yet only AEGIS has been evaluated there; (b) MuJoCo 3+ natively supports SDF computation from meshes, reducing implementation barriers; (c) DFM-VLA (Mar 2026) demonstrates that iterative action refinement within VLA is feasible and effective — our SDF-gradient refinement provides a collision-specific instantiation of this paradigm.

## Landscape (SOTA & Limitations)

3D-AWARE VLAs (improve spatial reasoning, do NOT target collision avoidance): DepthVLA (arXiv 2510.13375, Oct 2025) integrates a pretrained depth transformer via mixture-of-transformers, achieving 94.9% on LIBERO but not evaluated on collision metrics. QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836, Oct 2025) uses quantized depth prediction as VLA auxiliary supervision via VQ-VAE — the closest methodological precedent for auxiliary-task supervision, operating in 2.5D camera frame without collision-awareness; open-source on GitHub. GeoAware-VLA (arXiv 2509.14117, Sep 2025) injects pretrained geometric vision model features for viewpoint invariance. 3D-CAVLA (arXiv 2505.05800, May 2025) enhances task generalization via chain-of-thought reasoning, depth-aware perception, and ROI detection, achieving 98.1% on LIBERO in-domain; open-source on GitHub. AugVLA-3D (arXiv 2602.10698, Feb 2026, ICRA 2026) uses VGGT for depth-driven 3D feature augmentation with geometry-aware routing and action-assistant regularization. Evo-0 (arXiv 2507.00416, Jul 2025) uses VGGT geometric foundation model for implicit 3D understanding. SpatialVLA (arXiv 2501.15830, Jan 2025) introduces Ego3D position encoding. StemVLA (arXiv 2602.23721, Feb 2026) forecasts future 3D spatial geometry. SA-VLA (arXiv 2602.00743, Jan 2026) fuses implicit spatial representations for RL fine-tuning. ST-VLA (arXiv 2603.13788, Mar 2026) enables 4D spatiotemporal understanding. 3DS-VLA (2025) adds 2D-to-3D positional alignment. Evo-Depth (arXiv 2605.14950, May 2026) proposes lightweight depth-enhanced VLA. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276) proves implicit 3D alignment accelerates VLA training 3.8×. GST-VLA (arXiv 2603.09079, Mar 2026) uses Gaussian spatial tokens. COLLISION-SAFE VLAs (target collision avoidance but externalize safety): AEGIS/VLSA (arXiv 2512.11891, Dec 2025) is the only published collision-safe manipulation VLA, achieving 77.85% CAR on SafeLIBERO via plug-in CBF — but safety is post-hoc correction, not internalized reasoning. CoFreeVLA (arXiv 2601.21712, Jan 2026) addresses dual-arm self-collision via risk estimation, not obstacle avoidance. SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2503.03480) uses constrained MDPs for safety alignment via reward shaping, not geometric reasoning. ACTION REFINEMENT VLAs: DFM-VLA (arXiv 2603.26320, Mar 2026) demonstrates iterative action token refinement via discrete flow matching on LIBERO (95.7% success) — establishes feasibility of within-VLA action refinement but without collision-specific guidance. DIFFERENTIABLE SDF IN ROBOTICS (not VLA): SAMP (arXiv 2509.11185, Sep 2025) fuses robot+environment SDF on spatial anchors for neural motion policy with 7% collision reduction — demonstrates SDF-gradient-guided policy learning but is not a VLA. CSSDF-Net (arXiv 2603.18669, Mar 2026) learns C-space SDF for trajectory optimization. The April 2026 VLA safety survey (arXiv 2604.23775) confirms this gap.

## Proposed Approach

We propose ColliForce-VLA, whose primary contribution is a differentiable collision-aware action generation mechanism for VLAs, enabled by a learned workspace SDF that provides gradient-based collision guidance within the forward pass — not merely auxiliary supervision during training and not post-hoc trajectory correction. This is architecturally distinct from both QDepth-VLA (training-only auxiliary loss) and AEGIS (external CBF correction). Key insight: While depth auxiliary tasks (QDepth-VLA) teach the model 'how far each pixel is from the camera' with gradients in image space, our learned SDF predicts 'how close each 3D workspace point is to the nearest obstacle surface' with gradients in workspace frame — and crucially, these SDF gradients can flow back through the action generation pathway during the forward pass, directly modulating action tokens toward collision-free configurations. Architecture — three components with distinct roles: (1) SDF Decoder with Action-Gradient Coupling: A cross-attention decoder takes intermediate VLA backbone features (from π0 via openpi or OpenVLA-OFT) and predicts signed distance at sparse 3D query points (2048 points, importance-sampled near robot workspace and object surfaces). Ground-truth SDF is extracted from LIBERO/SafeLIBERO MuJoCo visual geometry meshes (OBJ/STL assets, not simplified collision convex hulls) using established mesh-to-SDF libraries (trimesh proximity queries, pysdf). Critical design choice: the SDF decoder shares intermediate representations with the action head via a bidirectional cross-attention bridge — SDF features inform action generation, and action token positions define where SDF is most needed. This creates an architectural coupling absent in QDepth-VLA's purely auxiliary decoder. (2) SDF-Gradient-Guided Action Refinement (PRIMARY NOVELTY): During the forward pass, predicted SDF values at candidate end-effector positions (derived from action tokens) are used to compute workspace-frame collision gradients via backpropagation through the SDF decoder. These gradients are projected back into the action token space through a learned linear projection, producing a collision-avoidance correction that is added to the action tokens before the final action head output. This is a single differentiable forward pass — not iterative post-hoc correction. The mechanism is end-to-end trainable: the SDF decoder learns to produce gradients that, when projected into action space, reduce collisions. Theoretical basis: ∇SDF at a point in workspace directly points away from the nearest obstacle surface (by definition of SDF), providing geometrically meaningful collision-avoidance direction. In contrast, depth gradients in camera frame encode ∂depth/∂pixel, which requires an implicit perspective-to-workspace coordinate transformation (involving camera intrinsics, extrinsics, and nonlinear projection) to yield collision-relevant workspace directions — this transformation degrades gradient quality, especially for oblique viewing angles and occluded regions. (3) SDF Auxiliary Loss (SECONDARY): Standard SDF prediction loss during training forces the backbone to internalize full 3D collision geometry including occluded regions. This provides the representational foundation for component (2) but is explicitly secondary — the key contribution is how SDF gradients modulate action generation, not the auxiliary loss itself. Training: Joint optimization of action prediction loss, SDF prediction loss, and an SDF-gradient alignment loss that encourages the gradient correction to reduce predicted collision probability. The gradient alignment loss is key: it ensures the learned SDF-to-action-space projection produces corrections that actually improve collision avoidance, not just minimize SDF prediction error. Evaluation strategy — two tiers: Tier 1 (Standard): SafeLIBERO (32 collision scenarios, 1600 episodes) measuring both collision avoidance rate (CAR) and task success rate (TSR), plus standard LIBERO suites to verify no regression. Tier 2 (Stress Tests — isolating SDF advantages over depth): We design supplementary scenarios in MuJoCo/LIBERO that specifically test SDF's claimed advantages: (a) Occluded-obstacle scenarios: obstacles placed behind the robot arm invisible to the single camera — depth cannot perceive them, SDF from 3D workspace knowledge can; (b) Dense-corridor scenarios: end-effector must navigate between closely packed objects where depth map gradients blur across multiple surfaces while SDF encodes distance to ALL nearby surfaces simultaneously; (c) Multi-angle proximity: scenarios where the camera viewing angle creates depth ambiguities (nearly parallel surfaces at similar depth) that SDF naturally resolves. These stress tests are designed so that if SDF wins convincingly on them — even with marginal gains on standard SafeLIBERO — the paper tells a compelling story about when and why SDF matters. Critical baselines: (1) QDepth-VLA (open-source GitHub) — depth-as-auxiliary-supervision, our closest methodological comparator and primary depth baseline; (2) AEGIS/VLSA — post-hoc CBF approach, current SOTA on SafeLIBERO; (3) Vanilla VLA (OpenVLA-OFT, π0) — no spatial auxiliary supervision; (4) Spatial Forcing — general 3D alignment; (5) DepthVLA — if code becomes available, otherwise secondary to QDepth-VLA. Key ablations: (A1) SDF auxiliary supervision only (no gradient-guided action generation) — isolates training-time benefit, directly comparable to 'QDepth-VLA with SDF target swap'; (A2) SDF-gradient-guided action generation only (no auxiliary loss during training, decoder trained separately then frozen) — isolates inference-time mechanism; (A3) Full ColliForce-VLA (both) — demonstrates synergy; (A4) SDF vs. depth vs. binary occupancy as auxiliary target, all with gradient-guided action generation — tests whether SDF gradients are specifically better than depth/occupancy gradients for collision avoidance; (A5) Ablation on SDF ground-truth source: visual mesh vs. collision convex hull — validates our design choice. Advantages of SDF-gradient-guided action generation over alternatives: (a) Workspace-frame gradients directly aligned with robot motion — no coordinate transformation needed; (b) Full 3D coverage including occluded regions; (c) Continuous, geometrically meaningful gradients — ∇SDF points away from obstacles by construction; binary occupancy has zero gradient almost everywhere; (d) Single forward pass — no iterative refinement or external correction loop; (e) End-to-end trainable — the entire pathway from SDF prediction to action correction is differentiable.

# ColliForce-VLA Related Work Literature Map

> Generated: 2026-05-19 | Project: diff_collision_sdf (ICLR 2027)

---

## Category 1: 3D-aware VLAs

These methods improve spatial reasoning via depth, geometry, or point cloud representations, but **none explicitly targets collision avoidance**.

| 论文 | Venue / arXiv | 日期 | 方法概要 | 关系 | Baseline? | 代码 |
|------|--------------|------|---------|------|-----------|------|
| QDepth-VLA | arXiv 2510.14836 | Oct 2025 | VQ-VAE量化深度预测作为VLA辅助监督任务 | `method-component` | **Yes** — 最近方法论对标，辅助监督范式直接可比 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ucasmichael/QDepth-VLA) |
| DepthVLA | arXiv 2510.13375 | Oct 2025 | Mixture-of-Transformers融合预训练深度Transformer与VLM | `baseline` | **Yes** — 深度增强VLA代表，若代码可用 | 未开源（声称将发布） |
| Spatial Forcing | ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276 | Oct 2025 | 隐式3D对齐VLA视觉表征与3D基础模型，训练加速3.8× | `baseline` | **Yes** — 隐式3D对齐SOTA，证明不需显式3D输入 | [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenHelix-Team/Spatial-Forcing) |
| SpatialVLA | RSS 2025, arXiv 2501.15830 | Jan 2025 | Ego3D位置编码+自适应空间对齐，1.1M真实数据训练 | `landscape` | No — 不同技术路线，related work讨论 | [GitHub](https://github.com/SpatialVLA/SpatialVLA) |

| Evo-0 | arXiv 2507.00416 | Jul 2025 | 插件式隐式3D几何特征模块(VGGT)，无需推理时3D输入 | `landscape` | No — 方法路线与Spatial Forcing类似 | [GitHub](https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/Evo-VLA) |
| GeoAware-VLA | arXiv 2509.14117 | Sep 2025 | 冻结预训练VGGT作为几何特征提取器替换标准图像编码器 | `landscape` | No — 视角泛化导向 | 未开源 |
| AugVLA-3D | ICRA 2026, arXiv 2602.10698 | Feb 2026 | VGGT深度驱动3D特征增强+action assistant正则化 | `landscape` | No — 3D增强路线，非碰撞导向 | 未开源 |
| StemVLA | arXiv 2602.23721 | Feb 2026 | 预测未来3D空间几何+时序注意力聚合历史4D表征 | `landscape` | No — 时空预测导向 | 声称开源，未找到repo |
| SA-VLA | arXiv 2602.00743 | Jan 2026 | 隐式空间表征融合+几何感知奖励+空间条件退火探索的RL微调 | `landscape` | No — RL微调框架 | 未开源 |
| ST-VLA | arXiv 2603.13788 | Mar 2026 | 2D引导→3D轨迹+空间掩码的分层4D时空理解 | `landscape` | No — 时空理解框架 | 未开源 |
| GST-VLA | arXiv 2603.09079 | Mar 2026 | 高斯空间Tokenizer生成128个3D各向异性高斯基元+DA-CoT | `landscape` | No — 新颖表征但非碰撞相关 | 未开源 |
| 3DS-VLA | CoRL 2025 | Aug 2025 | 2D-to-3D位置对齐+序列化3D空间约束定义抓取关键点 | `landscape` | No — 3D对齐方法 | 未开源 |
| Evo-Depth | arXiv 2605.14950 | May 2026 | 轻量深度增强VLA框架 | `landscape` | No — 轻量化深度增强 | 可能开源(MINT-SJTU组) |

### 详细分析

**必须对比的 Baselines (Cat 1):**

1. **QDepth-VLA** — 最关键的方法论对标。同样使用辅助3D监督范式（深度 vs. 我们的SDF），但(a)在2.5D相机空间操作，(b)解码器仅训练时使用无双向耦合，(c)无推理时梯度流。我们的消融A4（SDF vs depth vs binary occupancy作为辅助目标）直接与其对比。代码已开源，可复现。

2. **DepthVLA** — 深度增强VLA的另一代表，MoT架构。若QDepth-VLA为主要深度baseline则DepthVLA为次要，视代码可用性决定。

3. **Spatial Forcing** — 证明隐式3D对齐在VLA中有效的里程碑工作(ICLR 2026)。需展示我们的SDF梯度引导在碰撞场景优于通用3D对齐。代码已开源。

**整体观察:** 14篇3D-aware VLA中仅4篇有开源代码(QDepth-VLA, 3D-CAVLA, Evo-0, Spatial Forcing, SpatialVLA)。该领域快速扩张但代码开源率低。所有方法优化任务成功率/泛化能力，**无一报告碰撞指标**，验证了我们的research gap。

---

## Category 2: Collision-safe VLAs

这些方法**针对碰撞安全**，但通过外部后处理而非内化空间理解。

| 论文 | Venue / arXiv | 日期 | 方法概要 | 关系 | Baseline? | 代码 |
|------|--------------|------|---------|------|-----------|------|
| AEGIS/VLSA | arXiv 2512.11891 | Dec 2025 | 插件式CBF安全约束层：开集目标检测+深度→物理空间避障QP求解 | `direct-competitor` | **Yes** — SafeLIBERO上唯一已发表结果，CAR提升59.16% | [GitHub](https://github.com/THU-RCSCT/vlsa-aegis) |
| SafeVLA | NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2503.03480 | Mar 2025 | CMDP约束学习框架：安全正负样本对比学习，安全性提升83.58% | `baseline` | **Yes** — NeurIPS Spotlight，RL-based安全对齐代表 | [GitHub](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment/SafeVLA) |
| CoFreeVLA | arXiv 2601.21712 | Jan 2026 | 短时域自碰撞风险估计器+风险门控+恢复策略(双臂) | `orthogonal` | No — 双臂自碰撞，非环境障碍物避障 | 未开源 |

### 详细分析

**AEGIS/VLSA — 最重要的直接竞品:**
- **SafeLIBERO结果:** 是。AEGIS **创建了** SafeLIBERO基准(4 suites, 16 tasks, 32 scenarios, 1600 episodes)。报告CAR 77.85%, TSR提升17.25%。
- **代码状态:** 已开源 [GitHub](https://github.com/THU-RCSCT/vlsa-aegis)，含SafeLIBERO数据集 [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/datasets/THURCSCT/SafeLIBERO)。
- **与我们的核心对比:** AEGIS是后处理(post-hoc CBF correction)，不改变VLA内部空间理解。我们是前向传播内(forward-pass internalized SDF gradient)。在密集杂乱场景中，后处理方法的"安全修正空间"小，内化方法可实现"预见性回避"。
- **风险:** AEGIS作者(清华RCSCT)可能将安全层内化——需监控。

**SafeVLA — 重要baseline:**
- **SafeLIBERO结果:** 否。使用自建Safety-CHORES基准。
- **代码状态:** 已开源 [GitHub](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment/SafeVLA)，含HuggingFace模型。
- **与我们的区别:** RL-based约束学习(CMDP) vs. 我们的几何方法(SDF梯度)。两种safety alignment范式的对比本身是有价值的论文贡献点。

**CoFreeVLA:**
- 聚焦双臂自碰撞(self-collision)而非环境障碍物避障。与我们问题设定不同，仅需related work简要提及。

**SafeLIBERO基准现状:** 目前**仅AEGIS一家**在SafeLIBERO上有结果。这既是机会（我们的结果将是第二个），也意味着缺乏多方对比数据。

---

## Category 3: Differentiable SDF in Robotics

这些方法在传统机器人规划中使用可微分SDF，**非VLA方法**，为我们的技术组件提供基础。

| 论文 | Venue / arXiv | 日期 | 方法概要 | 关系 | Baseline? | 代码 |
|------|--------------|------|---------|------|-----------|------|
| SAMP | arXiv 2509.11185 | Sep 2025 | 空间锚点网格上统一编码环境+机械臂SDF，碰撞感知运动策略 | `method-component` | No — 非VLA，但SDF梯度引导策略学习的关键参考 | 未开源 |
| Prof. Robot | CVPR 2025, arXiv 2503.11269 | Mar 2025 | 可微分机器人渲染中集成神经碰撞分类器+Eikonal正则化 | `method-component` | No — 非VLA，可微分SDF用于碰撞优化的关键参考 | [GitHub](https://github.com/qrcat/prof.robot) |
| CSSDF-Net | arXiv 2603.18669 | Mar 2026 | C-space连续可微SDF，spatial-hashing数据生成，零样本泛化 | `landscape` | No — 传统运动规划 | 未开源 |
| iSDF | RSS 2022, arXiv 2204.02296 | Apr 2022 | 在线MLP从深度流学习3D坐标→签名距离，提供碰撞代价和梯度 | `method-component` | No — 实时神经SDF的奠基工作 | [GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/iSDF) |
| ReDSDF | IROS 2022, arXiv 2203.04739 | Mar 2022 | 正则化神经隐式距离场，任意尺度高维流形上的光滑距离场 | `method-component` | No — 反应式运动生成中SDF的关键参考 | [GitLab](https://git.ias.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de/ias_code/iros2022/redsdf) |
| Neural NMPC-SDF | IJRR 2025, arXiv 2511.21312 | Nov 2025 | 范围图像→潜向量→SDF解码，参数化NMPC碰撞约束 | `landscape` | No — 无人机导航，非操作 | [GitHub](https://github.com/ntnu-arl/sdf-nmpc) |
| CDFlow | arXiv 2509.13771 | Sep 2025 | Neural ODE建模C-space最小距离碰撞配置的完整分布 | `landscape` | No — C-space距离场理论工作 | 未开源 |
| CATNIPS | T-RO 2024, arXiv 2302.12931 | Feb 2023 | NeRF→Poisson点过程→概率碰撞约束+图搜索+样条优化 | `landscape` | No — 概率碰撞规避规划 | [GitHub](https://github.com/chengine/catnips) |

### 详细分析

**核心method-component参考:**

1. **SAMP** — 最接近我们技术路线的非VLA工作。在空间锚点上融合环境SDF+机器人SDF训练碰撞感知运动策略，碰撞率降低7%。证明SDF梯度可用于策略学习。我们将此范式迁移到VLA架构中。

2. **Prof. Robot** — CVPR 2025。证明可微分SDF可实现99%碰撞减少。Eikonal正则化确保梯度一致性的技术可借鉴。

3. **iSDF** — 实时神经SDF的奠基工作(Meta/Facebook Research)。在线从深度流训练MLP的范式与我们的SDF解码器设计相关。代码高质量开源。

4. **ReDSDF** — 正则化技术使SDF梯度场光滑，对我们的SDF-gradient-guided action refinement的梯度质量至关重要。

**整体观察:** SDF在机器人碰撞避障中的有效性已被充分验证(iSDF 2022 → SAMP 2025 → CSSDF-Net 2026)，但**所有工作都在传统运动规划框架内**，无一与VLA集成。这正是我们的gap。

---

| 论文 | Venue / arXiv | 日期 | 方法概要 | 关系 | Baseline? | 代码 |
|------|--------------|------|---------|------|-----------|------|
| DFM-VLA | arXiv 2603.26320 | Mar 2026 | 离散流匹配迭代精修动作token序列，LIBERO 95.7% | `method-component` | No — 证明VLA内动作精修可行，但无碰撞引导 | 未开源，[项目页](https://chris1220313648.github.io/DFM-VLA/) |

### 详细分析

**DFM-VLA** 证明了VLA内部迭代动作精修的可行性——我们的SDF-gradient-guided action refinement是此范式的碰撞特化实例。区别：DFM-VLA的精修是通用的(离散流匹配驱动)，我们的精修是碰撞引导的(SDF梯度驱动)且单次前向传播(非迭代)。
